research_leads.notes: Exact Facebook account is preserved. Public indexing/search did not produce a reliable real-world identity resolution or a reproducible Iran-war claim receipt in the reviewed corpus, so the lead remains IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED rather than guessed.

Public Telegram/X identity plus Press TV quotation/hosting relationship established. A bounded March 18–28 source-behavior review now records six distinct qualifying information events: Netanyahu-death speculation stated as fact, the F-35/F-15E misidentification, a recycled 2020 Sara Netanyahu video used as current-condition evidence, the two-missile/all-damage causal claim, scope mutation of Trump's energy-plant pause plus an unsupported invasion-motive attribution, and a population-wide 'lost public support' conclusion contradicted by representative polling. These incidents are counted at publication-event level, not per atomic proposition. The deterministic Bullshitter award must be derived, not manually assigned.

Facebook seed and public X identity @_IranMilitary_ resolve to the same account brand. Indexed June war coverage preserves declaratory/amplification messaging, but the reviewed sample does not establish a claim-level adverse incident. Real-world operator remains unknown.

Public identity resolves to Russell Ellis / Jolly Good Ginger. Iran-war commentary was found, including a March 2 DEFIANCE appearance, but the reviewed public material did not establish a specific canonical Atlas misinformation incident. Keep as LIMITED_RELEVANT_ACTIVITY unless later claim-first research produces an incident.

The transit-count substrate in the July 20 Hormuz commentary is substantially supported, but the article makes a distinct causal claim that successive U.S. strikes were themselves producing the shutdown. That inferential bridge is routed upstream for adjudication; accurate counts do not validate the causal explanation.

A bounded July 17–August 15 review now records six distinct qualifying MeidasTouch publication events. The recurring pattern preserves a severe factual substrate—Iranian vessel attacks, genuine U.S. munitions depletion, extensive base damage and Bahrain logistics disruption—while repeatedly converting that substrate into unsupported absolutes such as seven tankers destroyed, zero Patriot/THAAD inventory, the U.S. out of all weapons, and essentially all regional U.S. bases destroyed/obliterated. Repeated publications count separately; multiple atomic propositions inside one episode count once. The deterministic Bullshitter award must be derived rather than manually assigned. The older July 12 broad-base-destruction discovery remains separately queued for upstream canonical atomization and is not needed to earn the source-behavior award.
Reviewed Lincoln stories explicitly attribute Iranian claims and include U.S. non-confirmation/denial context.
Reviewed F-15E/CSAR examples are attributed/qualified reporting; no adverse incident found in the sampled canonical family.

Multiple Iran-war/public-affairs factual-claim surfaces are routed claim-by-claim. WOL-native evidentiary review records six qualifying unsupported/misleading presentation incidents from July 22 through August 6, plus a September 17 31-million-soldiers generalization. Project-owner direct body review additionally reports that Valenti used 'nuclear strike' literally for nuclear-warhead use against Iran and, in the July 27 missile episode, went beyond real interceptor triage to an unsupported motive theory that the U.S. permissively let strikes occur to provoke anger. Those body observations remain explicitly non-transcript provenance until exact captions/timestamps are recovered.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Publisher headline stated that Trump gave Saudi Arabia nuclear weapons.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: BREAKING: Trump gives SAUDI ARABIA NUCLEAR WEAPONS
Publisher promotional short repeats the episode title.
DOE describes a peaceful civil nuclear cooperation agreement and safeguards framework.
Reuters describes civil nuclear cooperation and proliferation concerns, not a weapons transfer.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Publisher title/promo plus contemporaneous U.S. Department of Energy and Reuters coverage of the July 22 U.S.-Saudi nuclear agreement.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The observable factual substrate was a Section 123 civil nuclear cooperation and safeguards agreement. No reviewed source supported transfer of U.S. nuclear weapons to Saudi Arabia.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: The title converts a civil nuclear-cooperation agreement into a literal nuclear-weapons transfer. The underlying agreement is real; the weapons-transfer conclusion is not supported by the reviewed record.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Presentation-level WOL behavior finding. Any canonical proposition about weapons transfer may still be routed to Claims Forensics separately.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Preserve canonical truth adjudication separately from WOL's source-behavior finding.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Publisher headline stated that Trump sent nuclear-armed jets toward Iran.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Trump sends NUCLEAR ARMED JETS towards Iran.
Public repost preserves the Valenti title and July 23 publication timing.
Contemporaneous analysis says the B-1 bombers heading to the region were no longer nuclear capable and carried conventional weapons.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Publisher headline plus contemporaneous reporting/analysis on the bomber deployment and the aircraft's nuclear status.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The observable deployment involved B-1 bombers. Contemporaneous reporting explicitly identified those aircraft as formerly, not currently, nuclear capable and discussed conventional payloads.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: A real bomber movement was converted into a claim that the aircraft were nuclear armed. No reviewed evidence supported nuclear weapons aboard the deployed aircraft.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Counts the title/presentation claim, not an inference about what the body later said.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Canonical weapon/deployment truth remains upstream; WOL records the unsupported public presentation.

body_review_context.observation: Valenti is reported to have explicitly described the aircraft as carrying nuclear warheads for use against Iran; the proposition is literal nuclear-weapon use, not merely nuclear-capable aircraft.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Publisher headline presented a Russian missile incursion/crash as 'Russia Bombs Poland.'

public_receipts.text_excerpt: BREAKING: Russia Bombs Poland ...
Publisher promotional short repeats the episode title.
Poland said a Russian missile violated its airspace and crashed, with no reason to believe Poland was the target.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Publisher title/promo and contemporaneous Reuters preservation of Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk's on-site assessment.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The supported substrate is a Russian missile crossing Polish airspace and crashing there during an attack on Ukraine. Poland's prime minister said there was no reason to believe Poland was the target.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: The title upgrades a documented incursion/crash during an attack on Ukraine into 'Russia Bombs Poland.' The attack-on-Poland implication is not supported by the reviewed evidence.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: The Russian origin and Polish impact are preserved as supported substrate; only the attack-on-Poland bridge is scored.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Any canonical NATO/Russia attack proposition remains an upstream truth-adjudication question.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Publisher headline stated that Trump cancelled a nuclear strike on Iran.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Trump CANCELS THE NUCLEAR STRIKE on Iran
Publisher promotional short repeats the nuclear-strike title.
Reuters reporting describes cancelled massive attacks/strikes, not use of a nuclear weapon.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Publisher title/promo plus contemporaneous Reuters reporting on the attack Trump said he had authorized and then called off.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: Contemporaneous reporting supports that Trump called off planned massive attacks on Iran. The reviewed record did not support a planned nuclear-weapon strike.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: This is a presentation finding. Body-level narrative remains separately body-gated.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Canonical attack-plan semantics remain upstream; WOL records the unsupported strength of the publisher headline.

body_review_context.observation: Valenti is reported to have used 'nuclear strike' literally to mean nuclear-warhead use against Iran, not a conventional strike on nuclear facilities.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: A genuine munitions-shortage story is preserved as the substrate; the whole-force zero-inventory generalization is the scored behavior.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Maps to the established F-15E/F-35 correction substrate without rewriting Claims Forensics.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Levins presented a 2020 video of Sara Netanyahu as if it reflected her current condition and used it to imply a recent drugged/depressed state.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Roya preserved Levins' March 21 wording and traced the video to November 3, 2020; it found no evidence supporting the drug-use implication.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Preserved Levins wording and the underlying video's provenance/date as reconstructed by Roya News.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The video was from 2020, not a recent wartime event, and the visual did not establish drug use.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: The scored behavior is the decontextualized presentation and current-condition inference, not the subjective word 'depressed' standing alone.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: One recycled/decontextualized media event; it is not split into separate recency and drug-state counts.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Preserve the recycled-media/current-condition proposition if a canonical family is later created.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Levins asserted that all same-day damage in Israel was caused by exactly two missiles and used that assertion to amplify a claim that Iran retained thousands more missiles.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Press TV preserved the attributed wording: all the damage today in Israel is because of 2 missiles; Iran has thousands more.
Independent public relay preserved the same attributed Levins wording.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: The two preserved attributed quotations plus public reporting on same-day strike damage and missile activity; search looked for site-by-site evidence tying all cited damage to exactly two impactors and for evidence connecting that observation to a ready remaining stockpile in the thousands.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: Visible damage is a factual substrate, but the preserved statement supplies no site-by-site attribution proving exactly two missiles caused all of it, and damage observations do not establish the size/readiness/composition of the remaining missile inventory.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: WOL does not need to prove that a different exact missile count caused the damage; the positive two-missile/all-damage causal assertion lacks the required evidentiary bridge.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Same publication event as existing discovery WOL-DISC-ETHAN-LEVINS-TWO-MISSILES-ALL-DAMAGE-20260322; count once despite two propositions.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Claims Forensics can still atomize causation and stockpile propositions separately.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Levins said Trump announced a 10-day ceasefire on civilian infrastructure, that Israel broke it within four hours, and that Israel was prolonging the war on purpose to force an American invasion.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Yahoo real-time preservation reproduces Levins' exact ceasefire/motive wording.
Trump's quoted language paused the period of energy-plant destruction by 10 days; it did not announce a general ceasefire on civilian infrastructure.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Levins' preserved March 27 statement and contemporaneous reporting quoting Trump's exact March 26 language about the ten-day pause.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: Trump's statement concerned a pause in destruction of Iranian energy plants, not a general civilian-infrastructure ceasefire. The source statement then added an intent claim that Israel acted to force a U.S. invasion without supplying evidence for that motive.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: One information event contains a scope mutation plus an unsupported intent attribution; it counts once.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Do not split the false scope expansion and motive attribution into two award incidents.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Canonical treatment may atomize ceasefire scope and intent separately.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Levins used anti-war demonstrations to conclude that Israel had lost public support for the Iran war.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Annahar preserved the exact Levins post and noted anti-war demonstrations were limited while most Israeli public opinion still supported the war.

Israel Democracy Institute reported 68% support in the total sample and over three-quarters support among Jewish respondents for continuing the operation; opposition among Jewish respondents was 11.5%.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Levins' preserved March 28 statement, contemporaneous protest reporting, and the Israel Democracy Institute's representative late-March survey.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The existence of anti-war demonstrations did not establish loss of public support. Contemporaneous representative polling still showed majority support for continuing the operation.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: The protest substrate was real; the population-wide conclusion was contradicted by the contemporaneous survey.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: This finding is about the factual generalization from protests to aggregate public support, not a judgment about the merits of the war.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Any broader public-opinion narrative family remains upstream.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Ben Meiselas stated that seven tankers had been destroyed by Iran in the preceding several days for using the U.S.-recommended southern route through Hormuz.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Transcript preserves the claim that seven tankers had been destroyed by Iran after using the U.S.-recommended southern route.
Reuters reported the U.S. said Iran had attacked seven commercial ships in the prior week; two Emirati oil tankers were struck, and Iran claimed two supertankers hit and disabled.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Meidas July 17 transcript plus contemporaneous Reuters reporting on the seven-vessel attack count and identified tanker damage.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The contemporaneous seven figure described commercial ships attacked, not seven tankers destroyed. Reuters identified two Emirati oil tankers struck and separately reported an Iranian claim that two supertankers were hit and disabled.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: A real seven-vessel attack count was converted into seven destroyed tankers. The event is scored at publication level once.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Do not collapse attacked, hit, disabled and destroyed into one maritime-loss metric.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Canonical maritime-loss accounting may atomize vessel identity and effect separately.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Meiselas said the U.S. had run out of PAC-3 Patriot interceptors and THAAD interceptors, lacked the needed Navy destroyers, and that Iran had obliterated U.S. military bases in the region.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Transcript preserves the zero-inventory Patriot/THAAD language and 'obliterated these US military bases' wording.

Reuters reported severe but nonzero defensive inventories: about 65% of Patriot interceptors expended and THAAD stocks at least 38% lower; ATACMS/PrSM were the classes described as virtually all used.

Pentagon watchdog accounting later described hundreds of buildings and structures damaged or destroyed at U.S. bases, preserving the distinction between installation damage and whole-base destruction.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Full Meidas episode transcript; Reuters inventory reporting based on internal U.S. data; later Pentagon-inspector-general accounting of regional base damage.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The underlying evidence supports severe depletion and severe facility damage. It does not support zero Patriot/THAAD inventory or a blanket conclusion that the regional U.S. bases were wholly obliterated.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: This is one information event containing repeated scope/zero-inventory generalizations; count once.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Preserve severe depletion and real base damage as factual substrate; score only the absolute/generalized conclusions.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Inventory classes and facility-level BDA remain separate canonical propositions.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Meiselas repeated that the U.S. was out of Patriot interceptors, out of THAAD interceptors and out of Navy destroyers, while saying regional bases had been abandoned and remaining undestroyed equipment moved to Israel.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Original MeidasTouch episode identity for the August 4 full podcast.
Transcript preserves repeated 'we're out of Patriot interceptors' and 'we're out of THAAD interceptors' wording.
Reuters reported approximately 65% Patriot expenditure and at least a 38% THAAD stock reduction, not zero stocks.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Original episode identity, full public transcript, and same-day Reuters reporting on U.S. missile/interceptor inventories.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: Same-day reporting supports severe depletion but directly distinguishes that from zero Patriot or THAAD inventory.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: This is a distinct later republication/repetition after the August 2 event and therefore counts separately under the repeated-publication rule.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Distinct August 4 repetition; do not deduplicate with August 2.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Canonical inventory readiness remains upstream; WOL scores the source's absolute presentation.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Meiselas said the United States was running out of all of its weapons, that Iranian ballistic missiles were hitting all their targets at U.S. bases, and that it was clear the U.S. had run out of interceptors and offensive weapons.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Full transcript preserves the 'runs out of all of its weapons,' 'all of its targets,' and 'run out of our interceptors and offensive weapons' claims.
Reuters documented class-specific severe depletion rather than all-weapons exhaustion.
Trump publicly acknowledged tighter supplies in some classes while describing other types as in very large supply; the statement does not validate an all-weapons-zero conclusion.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Full August 7 transcript, Reuters class-specific inventory reporting, and the direct August 6 presidential munitions statement.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: Evidence supports serious shortages in specified systems, not exhaustion of all U.S. weapons or all interceptors/offensive weapons. The transcript's own reasoning infers zero inventory from observed non-interceptions.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: The claim converts selective depletion and observed penetrations into universal inventory and interception conclusions.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Severe munitions shortfalls remain factual substrate; universal zero-inventory language is the scored bridge/conclusion.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Claims Forensics may separately adjudicate specific weapon-class inventories and specific missile engagements.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Meiselas said objectively the United States ran out of weapons in roughly 40 days, had basically abandoned all Middle East bases other than Israel, and that Iran obliterated the listed bases.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Original MeidasTouch episode identity for the August 11 full podcast.
Transcript preserves 'objectively, the United States ran out of weapons,' 'basically abandoned all of the Middle East bases,' and 'Iran obliterated those bases.'
Reuters' inventory reporting is severe but class-specific, not all-weapons exhaustion.
Pentagon watchdog accounting describes hundreds of structures damaged/destroyed at bases and logistics rerouting, rather than the blanket loss of essentially every regional base.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Original episode identity, full transcript, Reuters munitions reporting and the Pentagon-watchdog base-damage accounting later published by AP.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The evidence supports grave munitions shortages, extensive regional facility damage and logistics disruption. It does not establish that the U.S. literally ran out of weapons or that essentially every Middle East base except Israel was abandoned/obliterated.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: One August 11 publication event; multiple absolute conclusions within it do not multiply the incident count.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Counts once despite weapon-inventory and whole-base generalizations appearing together.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Canonical facility and inventory propositions remain independently atomizable.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Meiselas cited the real destruction of much of the Bahrain logistics base, then generalized across Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Iraq, Jordan, UAE and surrounding areas: 'The U.S. bases are destroyed.'

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Official podcast-feed page preserves episode identity and description that the U.S. was shutting down bases and moving logistics to Diego Garcia.
Transcript preserves the listed-country generalization and the sentence 'The U.S. bases are destroyed.'
The underlying report says Iran destroyed much of the Bahrain Navy base/logistics hub and forced Diego Garcia resupply; it does not say all listed regional bases were destroyed.
Pentagon-watchdog accounting describes hundreds of buildings and structures damaged or destroyed at bases across eight countries, preserving structure-level versus whole-installation scope.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Episode feed and full transcript, the underlying New York Times Bahrain logistics report cited in the episode, and the later Pentagon-watchdog regional damage accounting.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The cited/reporting substrate supports destruction of much of the Bahrain logistics hub and extensive damage across multiple installations. That does not establish the universal whole-base statement applied across the listed countries.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: This is a real-damage-to-universal-destruction scope mutation, not a denial that Iran inflicted major U.S. base damage.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Preserve Bahrain's severe/possibly mission-killing logistics damage separately from the blanket regional whole-base conclusion.
